summary: South Africa's draft national AI policy, published for public comment, cited academic references that did not exist, which experts attributed to AI hallucination. The government withdrew the draft and suspended officials pending investigation.
technical_summary: Drafters apparently used a generative AI tool whose output included invented journal articles and journals, and these were not verified before the draft was gazetted. Editors of named journals denied publishing the cited articles. The failure combines LLM hallucination with absent human fact-checking.

summary: A Polish radio station replaced human presenters with AI-generated ones and aired a simulated interview with a Nobel-winning poet who died in 2012. After public outcry and a petition, it ended the experiment.
technical_summary: Generative AI created virtual presenter personas and synthesized the voice of a deceased poet to conduct a fabricated interview, as a cost-cutting and audience-building experiment. Former hosts lost their jobs, and no consent from the poet or estate is described.

summary: Detroit police wrongfully arrested a Black man for larceny after a facial recognition match led them to him. He spent nearly three days in custody and the case was later dismissed. It was reportedly the second such Detroit case.
technical_summary: Police ran a still from a phone video through a face-matching program and treated a mismatched hit as an investigative lead. The man had tattoos and different features from the suspect, yet a photo lineup and warrant followed. Known higher error rates for darker-skinned faces and over-reliance on the match contributed.

summary: A 16-year-old stabbed three girls aged under 15 at a Finnish school, injuring them non-fatally. A manifesto attributed to him claimed he used ChatGPT while planning for about six months; police had not confirmed its authorship.
technical_summary: The attacker reportedly used a general-purpose chatbot as a planning aid over months. Later court reporting described hundreds of AI-related queries on topics including stabbing, anatomy and evading police. The AI did not act autonomously; this is a case of a chatbot being used in preparation for violence.

summary: A deepfake video falsely showed President Biden announcing a military draft of 20-year-olds for the war in Ukraine. It was shared on social media by political accounts and debunked by fact-checkers as AI-generated.
technical_summary: A synthetic video with AI-generated speech mimicked the US president announcing invocation of the Selective Service Act. It spread on Twitter through political commentators and partisan accounts before being debunked, illustrating how convincing audio-visual fakes can carry false policy claims.

summary: A Kenyan parliamentary committee found the public health insurer's AI claims system wrongly flagged legitimate hospital claims as fraudulent with too little human review, causing unjust denials and financial strain on hospitals.
technical_summary: The Social Health Authority's automated claims processing flagged genuine admissions as fraud, including during system downtime or over minor data mismatches, and rejected claims even with complete records. Hospitals lacked a transparent resubmission process, and the committee recommended mandatory human review of flagged claims.

summary: In 2020, with exams cancelled, a UK grading algorithm lowered nearly 40% of A-level results below teachers' assessments, hitting state schools harder than private ones. After an uproar, grades were reverted to teacher assessments.
technical_summary: Ofqual's standardization model combined teacher estimates and rankings with each school's grade history from the previous three years to keep results consistent with past years. This penalized strong students at historically lower-performing schools and favored small, private cohorts, producing systematic downgrading.
developers: UK Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation
